requirements.subject: ent:verdict-operation
requirements.canonical: A test verdict operation (`setverdict`, `getverdict`) IS an operation to set or retrieve a verdict.
requirements.original: Verdict operations given in table 29 allow to set and retrieve verdicts.

requirements.subject: ent:verdict-operation
requirements.canonical: A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions.
requirements.original: These operations shall only be used in test cases, altsteps and functions.

ambiguity.issue: Chose reading 1: 'functions' means functions that execute on a test component; verdict operations are not meaningful in the module control function (no local verdict). Also 'test cases' denotes testcase definitions.
readings: A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions executed on a test component, and SHALL NOT be used in the module control function or in functions called from it.
A test verdict operation SHALL only be used in testcases, altsteps and functions, including any function called from the module control function.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component of the active configuration SHALL maintain its own local verdict.
requirements.original: Each test component of the active configuration shall maintain its own local verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: A local verdict IS an entity owned by a single test component.
requirements.original: The local verdict is an object which is created for each test component at the time of its creation.

ambiguity.issue: 'object' is a glossary term for instances of classes (OO extension); the local verdict is not a class object.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: A local verdict IS created for each test component at the time of the creation of the test component.
requirements.original: The local verdict is an object which is created for each test component at the time of its creation.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: The local verdict IS used to track the individual verdict of each test component, i.e. of the MTC and of every PTC.
requirements.original: It is used to track the individual verdict in each test component (i.e. in the MTC and in each and every PTC).

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system IS instantiating and handling a global test case verdict.
requirements.original: Additionally, there is a global test case verdict instantiated and handled by the test system that is updated when each test component (i.e. the MTC and each and every PTC) terminates execution (see figure 14).

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-verdict
requirements.canonical: The test case verdict IS updated when a test component (the MTC or any PTC) terminates execution.
requirements.original: Additionally, there is a global test case verdict instantiated and handled by the test system that is updated when each test component (i.e. the MTC and each and every PTC) terminates execution (see figure 14).

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-verdict
requirements.canonical: The test case verdict IS NOT accessible to the `getverdict` and `setverdict` operations.
requirements.original: This verdict is not accessible to the getverdict and setverdict operations.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: When a testcase terminates execution, the testcase SHALL return the value of the test case verdict.
requirements.original: The value of this verdict shall be returned by the test case when it terminates execution.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-verdict
requirements.condition: the returned verdict is not explicitly saved in the control component
requirements.canonical: If the verdict returned by a testcase is not explicitly saved in the control component (e.g. assigned to a variable), then the returned verdict IS lost.
requirements.original: If the returned verdict is not explicitly saved in the control component (e.g. assigned to a variable) then it is lost.

requirements.subject: ent:start-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keywords `any` and `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `start` operation.
requirements.original: Operation: start (Table 28: neither any nor all allowed)

requirements.subject: ent:stop-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `all` MAY be used with the timer `stop` operation (e.g. `all timer.stop`).
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: yes; Example: all timer.stop

requirements.subject: ent:stop-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `any` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `stop` operation.
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: yes; Example: all timer.stop

requirements.subject: ent:read-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keywords `any` and `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `read` operation.
requirements.original: Operation: read (Table 28: neither any nor all allowed)

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `any` MAY be used with the timer `running` operation (e.g. `any timer.running`).
requirements.original: Operation: running; Allowed: yes; Example: if (any timer.running) {…}

requirements.subject: ent:running-timer-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `running` operation.
requirements.original: Operation: running; Allowed: yes; Example: if (any timer.running) {…}

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `any` MAY be used with the timer `timeout` operation (e.g. `any timer.timeout`).
requirements.original: Operation: timeout; Allowed: yes; Example: any timer.timeout

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-operation
requirements.canonical: The keyword `all` SHALL NOT be used with the timer `timeout` operation.
requirements.original: Operation: timeout; Allowed: yes; Example: any timer.timeout

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation IS the statement that sets the local verdict.
requirements.original: Table 29: Overview of TTCN-3 test verdict operations: Set local verdict; Col2: setverdict

requirements.subject: ent:getverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation IS the statement that gets the local verdict.
requirements.original: Table 29: Overview of TTCN-3 test verdict operations: Get local verdict; Col2: getverdict

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT specifying the actual mechanisms that update the local verdicts and the test case verdict.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: TTCN-3 does not specify the actual mechanisms that perform the updating of the local and test case verdicts.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The mechanisms that update the local verdicts and the test case verdict ARE implementation dependent.
requirements.original: These mechanisms are implementation dependent.

requirements.subject: ent:verdict
requirements.canonical: A verdict IS one of the five distinguished values of `verdicttype`: `pass`, `fail`, `inconc`, `none` and `error`.
requirements.original: The verdict can have five different values: pass, fail, inconc, none and error, i.e. the distinguished values of the verdicttype (see clause 6.1).

requirements.subject: ent:inconc-verdict
requirements.canonical: The verdict value `inconc` IS an inconclusive verdict.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: `inconc means an inconclusive verdict.`

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: When a test component is instantiated, the local verdict of the test component IS created.
requirements.original: When a test component is instantiated, its local verdict object is created and set to the value none.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: When a test component is instantiated, the local verdict of the test component IS initialized to `none`.
requirements.original: When a test component is instantiated, its local verdict object is created and set to the value none.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.condition: the local verdict is changed using setverdict
requirements.canonical: When the value of the local verdict is changed with the `setverdict` operation, the effect of the change SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
requirements.original: When changing the value of the local verdict (i.e. using the setverdict operation) the effect of this change shall follow the overwriting rules listed in table 30.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-verdict
requirements.canonical: The test case verdict IS implicitly updated on the termination of a test component.
requirements.original: The test case verdict is implicitly updated on the termination of a test component.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-verdict
requirements.canonical: The implicit update of the test case verdict on the termination of a test component SHALL follow the overwriting rules of table 30.
requirements.original: The effect of this implicit operation shall also follow the overwriting rules listed in table 30.

requirements.subject: ent:overwriting-rule
requirements.canonical: If the current verdict is `none`, assigning `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `none` IS resulting in the assigned value.
requirements.original: Table 30: Overwriting rules for the verdict (rows: current value None/Pass/Inconc/Fail; columns: new verdict assignment value pass/inconc/fail/none) None: pass inconc fail none

requirements.subject: ent:overwriting-rule
requirements.canonical: If the current verdict is `pass`, assigning `pass` or `none` IS resulting in `pass`, assigning `inconc` IS resulting in `inconc`, and assigning `fail` IS resulting in `fail`.
requirements.original: Table 30: Overwriting rules for the verdict (rows: current value None/Pass/Inconc/Fail; columns: new verdict assignment value pass/inconc/fail/none) Pass: pass inconc fail pass

requirements.subject: ent:overwriting-rule
requirements.canonical: If the current verdict is `inconc`, assigning `pass`, `inconc` or `none` IS resulting in `inconc`, and assigning `fail` IS resulting in `fail`.
requirements.original: Table 30: Overwriting rules for the verdict (rows: current value None/Pass/Inconc/Fail; columns: new verdict assignment value pass/inconc/fail/none) Inconc: inconc inconc fail inconc

requirements.subject: ent:overwriting-rule
requirements.canonical: If the current verdict is `fail`, assigning any of `pass`, `inconc`, `fail` or `none` IS resulting in `fail`.
requirements.original: Table 30: Overwriting rules for the verdict (rows: current value None/Pass/Inconc/Fail; columns: new verdict assignment value pass/inconc/fail/none) Fail: fail fail fail fail

requirements.subject: ent:error-verdict
requirements.canonical: The `error` verdict IS set by the test system to indicate that a test case error (runtime error) has occurred.
requirements.original: The error verdict is special in that it is set by the test system to indicate that a test case (i.e. runtime) error has occurred.

requirements.subject: ent:setverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `setverdict` operation SHALL NOT set the `error` verdict.
requirements.original: It shall not be set by the setverdict operation and will not be returned by the getverdict operation.

requirements.subject: ent:getverdict-operation
requirements.canonical: The `getverdict` operation IS NOT returning the `error` verdict.
requirements.original: It shall not be set by the setverdict operation and will not be returned by the getverdict operation.

requirements.subject: ent:error-verdict
requirements.canonical: A verdict value other than `error` CANNOT override an `error` verdict.
requirements.original: No other verdict value can override an error verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:error-verdict
requirements.canonical: An `error` verdict IS only obtainable as the result of an `execute` operation.
requirements.original: This means that an error verdict can only be a result of an execute test case operation.

ambiguity.issue: Chose reading 1 (error appears only as the return value of execute, since it cannot be set or read inside test components). 'execute test case operation' is not the name of the operation.
readings: An `error` verdict IS only observable as the value returned by an `execute` operation.
An `error` verdict IS only produced while a testcase started by an `execute` operation is running.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component SHALL maintain, together with its local verdict, an implicit charstring variable storing information about the reasons for assigning the verdict.
requirements.original: Together with the local test verdict, each test component shall also maintain an implicit charstring variable to store information about the reasons for assigning the verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.canonical: The implicit charstring variable SHALL NOT have any effect on the verdict overwriting rules.
requirements.original: The implicit charstring variable shall have no effect on the overwriting rules and on the calculation of the final test case verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.canonical: The implicit charstring variable SHALL NOT have any effect on the calculation of the final test case verdict.
requirements.original: The implicit charstring variable shall have no effect on the overwriting rules and on the calculation of the final test case verdict.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: On the termination of a test component, the local verdict of the test component SHALL be logged together with the implicit charstring variable.
requirements.original: On the termination of the test component, the local verdict of the test component shall be logged together with the implicit charstring variable.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.canonical: The implicit charstring variable CANNOT be retrieved or read by any TTCN-3 language construct.
requirements.original: The implicit charstring variable cannot be retrieved and read by any TTCN-3 function, it only provides additional information for logging.

ambiguity.issue: 'TTCN-3 function' is meant as any TTCN-3 language construct (statement, operation, predefined or user-defined function).

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-charstring-variable
requirements.canonical: The implicit charstring variable IS only providing additional information for logging.
requirements.original: The implicit charstring variable cannot be retrieved and read by any TTCN-3 function, it only provides additional information for logging.
